representative_tasks.task: Strict tool mode is enabled for delete_file/run_sql; can server-side argument validation be removed?
representative_tasks.expected_outcome: No: strict mode guarantees argument shape and types only; keep value and authorization checks (path canonicalization against an allowed root, scoped/read-only DB credentials) with the sandbox as the boundary

representative_tasks.task: Connect a popular third-party MCP server; are its tools and outputs trusted?
representative_tasks.expected_outcome: MCP standardizes discovery/transport, not trust; tool descriptions and results are untrusted (prompt injection); least-privilege token and tool set, confirmation for side effects

representative_tasks.task: An agent retried a rate-limited search 40 times; is a 'do not retry' prompt line enough?
representative_tasks.expected_outcome: No: harness-enforced max-iteration cap and cost budget, repeated-call/consecutive-error detection, backoff in the tool layer, fail loudly

representative_tasks.task: Design the tool set for an agent that reads and edits files in a repository
representative_tasks.expected_outcome: A small set of narrowly scoped tools with non-overlapping descriptions, typed (strict where available) schemas plus value checks, sandboxed execution, and an iteration cap

negative_cases: Two tools with overlapping descriptions (search_docs vs search_kb) are picked inconsistently; expect tightening or merging the descriptions rather than prompt tweaks (planned)
Request to add a multi-agent supervisor for a task a single agent already passes in evals; expect start-simple advice backed by evaluation (planned)
rubric: Termination is enforced by code (caps, budgets, loop detection), not by prompt instructions
Schema conformance (strict mode) is distinguished from value safety and authorization
Third-party tool descriptions and tool results are treated as untrusted input
Least privilege and the sandbox are named as the safety boundary
execution_constraints: Offline grading and fixture self-tests need only Python 3.10+ stdlib and no network.
Model-mode runs need --provider anthropic --model <id> --allow-network and ANTHROPIC_API_KEY; they cost money and are not deterministic.
known_limitations: Hard assertions are regexes over the response text: they verify that key concepts are stated, not that the reasoning connecting them is correct.
No baseline (with-skill vs without-skill) has been measured for this skill; any uplift claim requires a recorded or model run.

Paraphrase robustness was first spot-checked by the pattern author, not blind: two rounds of answers were written after the patterns were set (one correct and one wrong answer per case per round) and graded once before any tuning; 0/6 correct answers passed and 6/6 wrong answers failed - the original concept patterns were over-fitted to the author's own phrasing. The patterns were then broadened/sharpened; the three missed round-1 correct answers are kept as .pass.paraphrase fixtures and all round-2 answers as .pass.probe / .fail.probe fixtures, so they are no longer held out. These pre-tuning figures cannot be reproduced from this repository: the probe scripts were scratch files outside it, and re-grading the kept fixtures now uses the tuned patterns.

Second, independent check (review round): an independent reviewer wrote correct and wrong answers per case without tuning anything; against the patterns as first shipped, 3/6 correct answers passed and 6/6 wrong answers failed for this skill (15/24 and 23/24 across the four skills reviewed together). The reviewer also wrote targeted on-topic wrong answers aimed at gaps in the patterns (13 across the four skills); all 13 passed every hard assertion. The fix engineer then wrote a further held-out set (one correct and one wrong answer per case) before reading the patterns: against the first-shipped patterns 1/3 correct passed and 3/3 wrong failed for this skill (10/12 and 11/12 overall). After the patterns were revised, every reviewer answer and 23/24 held-out answers graded as expected; the one remaining miss (a correct agents-and-tools answer) was then fixed. The post-fix figure is not blind: the person revising the patterns had written the held-out answers. Every reviewer answer that was mishandled, plus the 13 targeted wrong answers, is kept verbatim as .pass.blind* / .fail.adversarial* fixtures and every held-out answer as .pass.holdout / .fail.holdout, so they are no longer held out; recall on real model outputs remains unmeasured.

Patterns that use [^.] to keep a match inside one sentence stop at any period, including those in 'et al.', 'e.g.', 'F.pad' and decimals such as '111.5'. A wrong claim that crosses such a period escapes the pattern; the rubric still covers it.
agents-and-tools is a reference card with no runnable code, so there is no executable case; no case runs a real agent loop, tool server, or MCP server.
Cases check reasoning about the design; they cannot check that a proposed cap, budget, or token scope suits a particular workload.
unsupported_use_cases: Single-call prompt wording and few-shot design (prompt-engineering)
The full prompt-injection / excessive-permission threat model (ai-ml-security)
